key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates degradation under thermal aging, with losses extending into the perovskite bulk.
engineering_relevance: Nondestructive, depth-sensitive monitoring can help engineers distinguish initial interface-passivation benefits from long-term thermal stability risks.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe interface- and bulk-dominated photoluminescence responses.
Compare PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks before and during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decay signatures using diffusion-recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination associated with fullerene deposition after treatment, followed by faster thermal degradation; simulations support interpreting the wavelength-dependent signatures through surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
watch_item: Depth attribution is model-supported rather than a direct depth measurement, and the abstract provides no quantitative device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
